summary: effectiveEnvironmentDigest bakes in whatever ad-hoc env vars a command was run with, so a genuinely fresh PASS can still fail the next admissibility check.
trigger: B-3144: ran done_required_validate with LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS/LATTICE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS env-var overrides set (needed for an earlier, much longer 94-command validate step, not actually needed for this specific 2-command check whose default budget was already generous). Those extra env vars got hashed into the evidence's effectiveEnvironmentDigest (core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment). story_advance --phase=DONE then recomputed the digest WITHOUT those vars and refused with effective-environment-digest-mismatch[0]/[1] -- this happened even on a second, genuinely fresh done_required_validate re-run, because I made the same env-var mistake twice before noticing.
lesson: Do not set ad-hoc env-var overrides (LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, LATTICE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, or any other ad-hoc export) on a done_required_validate/validate call unless that SPECIFIC command actually needs a longer budget than its own configured default. Extra env vars are not free -- they get baked into the admissibility digest and will mismatch the next consumer's recomputation, which does not see your shell's exported vars. Check the command's own default timeoutMs first (shown in validate's own progress output) before reaching for an env override.
reusePrompt: Seeing 'Cannot enter DONE: ... effective-environment-digest-mismatch' after a fresh-looking PASS? Check whether the producing command had extra LATTICE_*_TIMEOUT_MS or other env vars exported that the checking command does not have.

summary: A test fixture that 'poisons' state via a synthetic/fake identifier can be silently defused by an unrelated later fix that specifically targets fake or mismatched identifiers.
trigger: B-3144: injectPoisonedDuplicates/appendDuplicatesForRunId (in quorum-submit-smoke.ts) simulated the B-bf52 poisoning incident by tagging duplicate host_verdict rows with a synthetic non-current materialDigest string. B-f88e -- an unrelated, independently-landed sibling fix merged in via main the same day -- added a floor-side guard (eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade liveIdentities skip) that specifically declines to downgrade a stale-material duplicate sharing identity with an already-native verdict. That guard silently neutralized the synthetic-drift fixture: the poisoning stopped reproducing and 3 regression checks (including 2 guarding real security findings F-024/F-025) started passing vacuously, with no test failure to signal it.
lesson: After landing ANY defense-in-depth fix (especially one that specifically detects/ignores fake, stale, or mismatched data), re-audit sibling test fixtures elsewhere in the codebase that simulate the SAME attack/incident class via a similarly-shaped fake identifier -- they may now be silently defused and passing vacuously. This is invisible from a green test run; it only surfaces by re-deriving what the fixture is supposed to prove and checking the fixture still forces that exact condition (e.g. temporarily reverting the new fix and confirming the fixture-under-test genuinely fails again).

summary: verification_evidence_add's per-intentRef command pin is permanently immutable, and custom intentRefs must still resolve to an authored PLAN-time verificationIntent -- there is no way to add or strengthen mechanical evidence for a checklist item once REVIEW finds a weak check.
trigger: A REVIEW-phase test-coverage reviewer found 3 verificationIntent entries whose pinned command+selector couldn't actually discriminate the scenario it claimed to test (e.g. a git-diff substring check that would also match a REMOVED line, so it can't tell 'preserved' from 'deleted').

It also refuses a brand-new custom intentRef with intent_ref_unresolved unless that ref matches an intent already authored in checklist.json's verificationIntent arrays at PLAN time -- there is no command to append a NEW intent slot to an existing checklist item during REVIEW. When a reviewer finds a weak/non-discriminating pinned check post-hoc, the only real remedy is: (1) check whether a SIBLING intent on the same item already does the strong version of the same check (if so, cite it and resolve as sound-but-redundant); (2) if no sibling exists, independently re-verify the underlying claim by hand right now (a throwaway script/fixture) and record that manual re-verification plus the tooling gap explicitly in the finding_resolve reasoning -- do not try to force a mechanical re-pin, it will just error.

summary: A new lifecycle-gate artifact written OUTSIDE .lattice/story/actives/<storyId>/ needs its own runtime-artifact-registry entry (materialHash:'exclude') -- autoCommitStoryMetadata never reaches it, and auto-committing the write directly is the wrong fix (moves HEAD, breaks other signed evidence freshness).
trigger: B-a7c5 CHK-003's dev_memory_finish_decision writes to .lattice/dev-memory/finish-decisions/<storyId>.json, deliberately outside the story dir (it's shared dev-memory infrastructure, not per-story metadata). Left uncommitted after a write, this file fell through dirty-worktree classification to unexpected_dirty_files (blocking) and stranded review_run_start -- found live during REVIEW round 3.
lesson: First instinct was to auto-commit the write inside the handler (mirroring finding_resolve's commitHint/autoCommitStoryMetadata pattern) -- this worked for the immediate symptom but introduced a WORSE regression: the new commit moved HEAD, which retroactively invalidated any test-evidence.json/delivery-check.json already signed against the prior HEAD (stale_delivery_check materialHash mismatch), confirmed via a targeted repro before landing. The correct fix is almost always to register the path in core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts (RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY) with materialHash:'exclude', which routes dirty-worktree classification to the non-blocking runtime_artifact_changes category via findRuntimeArtifactEntry, AND ensures the path never perturbs currentMaterialHash in the first place -- no commit-timing/HEAD-movement side effects at all. Only add ignorePatterns if the artifact should ALSO be gitignored; a deliberately git-tracked-but-non-authoritative artifact (like this one) should have ignorePatterns:[] so it stays visible/shareable while still being non-blocking.
reusePrompt: review_run_start / dirty-worktree unexpected_dirty_files / new artifact outside story dir / stale_delivery_check materialHash mismatch after auto-commit / RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY materialHash exclude

summary: A materialHash-invariance test that only writeFileSync's (never commits) is non-discriminating: currentMaterialHash reads git ls-tree (committed state), so the assertion passes identically whether or not a runtime-artifact-registry exclusion actually exists.
trigger: B-a7c5's own F-005 regression test (added to prove a new registry exclusion works) only wrote the file, never committed it. A REVIEW quality-lane reviewer caught this in round 4 (F-006): deliberately removing the registry entry and re-running the test showed it still passed, because a bare write never touches HEAD/git ls-tree regardless of whether the exclusion exists.
lesson: When writing a regression test for a materialHash-exclusion fix, the test MUST actually commit the artifact (git add + git commit) and check currentMaterialHash across that commit -- not just before/after a bare write. A write-only invariance check only proves 'writing this file doesn't dirty an in-memory hash', which is trivially true for ANY uncommitted file regardless of registry configuration. Verify a new discriminating assertion's power directly: temporarily break the fix it's supposed to protect, confirm the test fails, then restore and confirm it passes again -- do not trust that an assertion is discriminating just because it currently passes.

summary: lattice.config.json's validate.commands does NOT cover every test file in the repo -- the project's root npm test (full-suite-runner.js, driven by package.json's much longer test:serial-reference script list) is a broader, separate canonical test command that can catch regressions lattice validate and multiple REVIEW rounds all miss.
trigger: B-a7c5's CHK-001 change (a new gate check running before proofStoryDevGateFailure) broke packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.ts's DEV-admission assertions. 5 REVIEW rounds (4 lattice-review-quality passes + full lattice validate 96/96 green each time) never caught it, because that file is not registered in lattice.config.json's validate.commands. A round-5 quality reviewer caught it only by going beyond the two named fixes under review and running the project's root npm test as due diligence.
lesson: lattice validate (and by extension every REVIEW round that relies on it as its evidence) only exercises whatever is explicitly listed in lattice.config.json's validate.commands array. The project's root package.json 'test' script (full-suite-runner.js) runs a much longer, separately-maintained list that is NOT a subset check against validate.commands -- a file can exist in one list, the other, both, or neither. For any change touching a widely-shared code path (state-machine guards, core registries, shared handler utilities), run the project's root npm test at least once before DONE, not just lattice validate. Also: npm test's own HEAD-drift self-protection aborts the whole run if anything commits mid-run (e.g. a concurrent dev_memory_capture/finding_resolve auto-commit) -- run it with zero concurrent git-mutating commands, or its own protective abort looks like a mass test failure when it is not.

summary: A test's generic top-level assertion failure message can mask the REAL underlying cause -- don't trust a surface error message as the root cause without tracing what actually happened first, especially when triaging a test as 'unrelated pre-existing' to justify not fixing it.
trigger: done-premerge-mainsha-recheck-smoke.ts failed with 'abort: external-advance shim fired (marker written) / the merge-tree interception marker was never created' -- I concluded this was an unrelated, pre-existing merge-tree-shim timing bug (confirmed the file wasn't in my diff, spawned a separate task to fix it). A round-6 quality reviewer added debug instrumentation and found the REAL cause: my own CHK-003 change (a new canFinishGuard check) was blocking the fixture's real story_advance DONE call with missing_dev_memory_finish_decision, BEFORE the story_advance call ever reached the merge-tree pre-check logic the fixture's assertion message was actually about. The fixture's assertion just checks 'did the expected marker get written', which is equally false whether the merge-tree logic never ran OR ran and failed differently -- the message doesn't distinguish those cases.
lesson: When a test fails with a message that sounds infrastructure/environment-related ('shim fired', 'marker never created', 'injection did not run'), and you're tempted to conclude 'unrelated, pre-existing, out of scope' -- verify by tracing the ACTUAL execution path (add temporary debug logging, or read the CLI's real stdout/stderr before the fixture's own assertion wrapper summarizes it), not just by checking 'is this file in my diff'. A file being untouched by your diff does NOT mean your diff didn't break it -- a new gate/check anywhere in the shared call path the file exercises can block it before it ever reaches the logic its own assertions describe. This is the same root-cause class as F-008 (a new gate running before pre-existing code the test expects to reach), just with a MORE misleading surface symptom this time.

summary: execFileSync's pipe-based stdio capture truncates large synchronous crash dumps at 8192 bytes on macOS; spawnSync with a real file descriptor does not.
trigger: Writing a RED reproduction script that captures a large child-process crash dump (a big JSON diagnostics payload embedded in an assert.equal custom message) via execFileSync, then grepping the captured text for a signature that appears near the END of the dump -- the grep silently fails to match because the capture was truncated well before reaching it, with no truncation warning.
lesson: execFileSync's internal pipe-based stdout/stderr capture can silently truncate a large synchronous write from a crashing child process at a small fixed size (observed: exactly 8192 bytes) on macOS, well below its documented maxBuffer default (1MB) -- this is NOT a maxBuffer issue, it is a pipe-buffer/flush-timing issue specific to large synchronous writes right before process exit. The fix: use spawnSync with stdio wired to a real file descriptor (fs.openSync a temp file, pass its fd as stdio[2]) instead of 'pipe', then read the file back with fs.readFileSync -- this captures the full output reliably. Always verify a RED script's assertions actually match by writing captured output to a file and grepping it directly during authoring, not just trusting a truthy exit code.
reusePrompt: Writing a script that captures a child process's crash output via execFileSync and a downstream regex/grep against it isn't matching a string you can see is really there in a manual run / RED script assertion mysteriously fails to match text that should be present in a large crash dump / execFileSync output looks truncated

summary: Rerouting a lock/path argument at a call site can be a no-op if the callee already independently re-derives the same shared root internally.
trigger: Diagnosing a worktree-teardown race by tracing WHERE a lock or path is passed in from, then patching that call site to pass a 'more correct' root, without first checking whether the callee already resolves to the same canonical location on its own.
lesson: acquireStoryTransitionLock(root, storyId) looked like it needed a stable-root reroute to survive a winning DONE deleting the worktree it was called from -- but storyTransitionLockPath already resolves root through resolveSharedLockRoot (git-common-dir based, B-d877 R2 FIX B) BEFORE touching disk, so ANY root string passed in (worktree path or main repo root) resolves to the identical shared lock directory. The reroute compiled, built, and even made the target smoke test pass -- because the REAL fix (a separate StoryArtifactMissingError translation) was landed in the same commit, masking that the reroute itself did nothing. A REVIEW reviewer caught it by comparing storyTransitionLockPath(worktreePath, id) vs storyTransitionLockPath(mainRepoRoot, id) directly and finding them identical. Before adding a 'fix' that reroutes an argument into a shared/lock/root-resolution function, read the CALLEE's own resolution logic first -- if it already normalizes via git-common-dir or similar, the caller-side reroute is redundant. When a test passes after a multi-part fix, that does not mean every part of the fix is load-bearing; isolate and re-test each part before crediting it as the actual fix.
reusePrompt: adding a stable-root/shared-root reroute before a lock or path helper / lock directory disappears with worktree teardown / fix passes tests but reviewer says a change is a no-op / multi-part fix, unclear which part is load-bearing

summary: verification_evidence_add pins a checklist intents evidence command+selector IMMUTABLY on the first selector-bearing write, forever - never bind a selector that embeds a value expected to change (like an assertion count).
trigger: Wrote a selector like "smoke passed: 27 assertions" for 32 verificationIntent items before all coverage was implemented. Later REVIEW findings required adding real assertions (27->33->40->45), and the selector permanently stopped matching - no verification_evidence_add/_batch_add call can ever change a pinned commands command or selector again, even nonMechanicalReason still requires the immutable command to match.
lesson: The only recovery once a bad selector is pinned: go back to PLAN phase and wholesale-replace the affected items verificationIntent via checklist_update (item.verificationIntent = args.verificationIntent is a full overwrite, which clears the embedded .verification pin field on each intent object - confirmed empirically). Then re-pin fresh with a selector that is a STABLE SUBSTRING PREFIX only (e.g. "smoke passed:" not "smoke passed: 27 assertions") so it survives future legitimate growth. kind:waiver bypasses the pin check entirely and satisfies REVIEW-phase gates but NOT the DEV->TEST verification-coverage gate or the DONE ProofStory-acceptance-binding completeness gate, both of which require genuinely mechanical (non-waiver) evidence.
reusePrompt: Seeing receipt-command-mismatch or receipt-selector-mismatch ("the verification pin is immutable") on verification_evidence_add/_batch_add? Or a checklist item stuck needing real coverage after its evidence was already pinned to a stale selector? Search for this lesson.

summary: done_prepare has a convergence invariant that fails if the SAME validation group (commandSetHash+materialHash+storyFilesHash) was executed more than once after TEST entry - repeated retries of a flaky done_required_validate/lattice validate under load pollute unchangedSuiteExecutions.
trigger: done_required_validate kept failing on an unrelated, load-sensitive pre-existing test (different test each time - flow-stability-smoke, review-pass-discard-smoke, validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke - all confirmed passing in isolation, load average was 8-40 on a shared dev machine with multiple concurrent worktree sessions). Retried the SAME command 3+ times at the same material hash until it finally passed. done_prepare --dryRun then failed with done_prepare convergence invariant failed: {unchangedSuiteExecutions:1,...} even though DONE-required validation itself showed PASS.
lesson: unchangedSuiteExecutions counts EXTRA executed terminals for the same validation group within the post-testEntry window (Math.max(0, postTestExecuted.length-1)), so any retry of a flaky validate/done_required_validate at unchanged material after TEST entry poisons it. The only recovery is bouncing the story TEST->DEV->REVIEW->TEST (with no code change) which resets facts.testEntryAt to NOW, excluding all prior executions from the window. REVIEW->DEV requires dev_memory_preflight_ack first (missing_dev_memory_preflight_ack). After the bounce, run done_required_validate/lattice validate EXACTLY ONCE at the new anchor and do not retry even if it fails - if it does fail, bounce again rather than retrying, since a retry-then-pass at the SAME anchor still leaves 2 executions in the window. Prefer waiting for system load to drop (check uptime) before that one critical attempt.
reusePrompt: Seeing "done_prepare convergence invariant failed" with a nonzero unchangedSuiteExecutions (or postTestReviewerReattestations/metadataRollbacks/humanConfirmations) after done_required_validate/lattice validate finally passed post-retries? Search for this lesson before assuming DONE is close.

summary: Hot-main DONE: after merging an actively-moving main, re-run a fresh validate to rewrite canonical evidence to the post-merge head so the net-diff lineage is clean, then autopilot/floor/delivery re-bind at the new materialHash.

summary: A guarantee restated in prose next to the code it describes goes stale, and each fix's own new prose carries the next instance.
trigger: You are about to write or repair a comment, docstring or decision document that states a property of nearby code - a bound, a count, a cap, an invariant, or what a function cannot do.
lesson: B-3434 spent twelve review rounds and forty-one findings on ONE defect wearing eight costumes: wrong values, a duplicated details copy the bound ignored, key names the bound did not cover, a GUARANTEED paragraph the code did not provide, the serialization boundary, the try/catch scope, an inherited prototype, and a work order that prescribed the very duplication it declared closed. Round 9 - the round reviewing round 8's fix - produced six more findings, every one in prose round 8 had written to close the class. Two rules came out of it. FIRST: make the property derived rather than remembered, and put the guarantee at the boundary it is claimed about; where it cannot be derived, DELETE the claim rather than narrow it, because a narrower false sentence is still false and a pointer to the function that owns the property cannot go stale. Deletion was the fix that finally held, three separate times. SECOND: never restate a measured number in prose. Five instances here were hand-typed figures that drifted - a cap of 200 restated 250 lines from its slice(0,200), a 'low hundreds of bytes' ceiling measured at 2030, a count of 'two routes' that went stale within the same session when a third arrived, and a table-row citation of verifier.ts:972-981 that the fix's own three added comment lines pushed to 975-984. Derive the figure from the constant, or point at the assertion that measures it.
reusePrompt: About to write a comment or doc that states what nearby code guarantees, or to type a number into prose? Search this: claim wider than code, derived not remembered, delete rather than narrow.

summary: When repeated repair rounds keep finding the same defect class, the boundary is usually wrong, not the fix - declare a stopping rule in advance and honour it.
trigger: A third or later repair round in the same seam finds a defect of the same shape as the ones before it.
lesson: Before round 8 I pre-committed in writing: if the next round finds another FUNDAMENTAL defect in the bounding machinery, CHK-004 switches to outcome B - ship the ceiling, diagnostics and regression tests, downgrade the bounding to what it actually is, commit a rationale, and move the guarantee to its own story. Round 9 found five more, and two review lanes plus the cross-vendor reviewer independently recommended the same extraction. The decisive fact was structural rather than about effort: the guarantee needed a writer-owned serialize-measure-write boundary in core/store.ts, and that file was outside the story's allowedModify - so no amount of care on this side of the seam could build it. Declaring the rule in advance is what made stopping a decision rather than a retreat, and stating the reason as scope rather than as difficulty is what made the follow-up scopeable. Two mechanics that mattered: check FIRST that no immutable pinned selector binds to the claim you are about to withdraw - none of B-3434's 24 pins asserted a guarantee, which is why outcome B was compatible with every receipt - and resolve the deferred findings as partially_mitigated with the transcripts, not as fixed.

summary: Cross-vendor review caught what four Claude lanes missed in four consecutive rounds, but its findings gate nothing until a lane reproduces them.
trigger: Running a real codex exec review as host-B alongside Claude reviewer lanes, or deciding whether cross-vendor review is worth its cost.
lesson: Six genuine codex exec reviews ran against B-3434. In four consecutive rounds codex found a real defect that four Claude lanes at the same revision had missed, including one inside a correction written to fix the previous one: the double-serialization divergence (reported 82 bytes, 36,000,077 on disk through the real StoryStore), the unguarded builder retry inside measureWith's catch, the false claim that the writer-owned boundary made F-036 moot when the reduction loop runs upstream of any writer, and a work-order remedy prescribing measurePersistedEvidenceBytes - the duplicated store format that F-033 identifies - in the same paragraph that declared F-033 closed. That last one was in wording I passed through verbatim without reading it back against F-033. So the cost is repaid on documentation-only rounds too, not just code rounds. The gap: isReviewerAgent requires a registered reviewerLane, and cross-host findings are filed under main, which has none - so they gate NOTHING. The working protocol is to have the owning Claude lane reproduce each claim BY EXECUTION and refile under its own lane, crediting codex explicitly as first surfacer so its work is not laundered; a lane that cannot reproduce a claim must decline to file it.

summary: The validate suite sits about 2 percent under its 900s watchdog, so registering any command tips it over - and the env override that rescues it is baked into the admissibility digest.
trigger: lattice validate or story_advance aborts with 'exceeded max timeout 900000ms', or you are about to add an entry to validate.commands.
lesson: Measured on B-3434: 96 commands summed to 879,647 ms and finished at 889.7s, roughly a one percent margin. Registering one additional 3.5s RED harness took it to 97 commands and 931,983 ms, and the next run aborted with no evidence written. commandCliMaxBudget in core/done-required-timeout-budget.ts gives done_required_validate and done_prepare a config-DERIVED budget but hands validate and story_advance a flat 15*60_000 default, which silently goes stale as the suite grows; quorum-submit-smoke alone is 317s, 36 percent of the whole suite. The workaround is LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, which effectiveCommandCliMaxBudget honours as an explicit override - but it is NOT in VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEY_LIST, so it is baked into effectiveEnvironmentDigest and will mismatch the next consumer's recomputation. Set it ONLY on the standalone validate, never on a gate command: assessStoredValidationPassAdmissibility checks command, JSON validity, allPass, coverage snapshot, freshness bindings and dirty tree - and NOT the environment digest - so a standalone run under a raised watchdog still produces a stored PASS that story_advance will reuse and skip the rerun.
reusePrompt: validate aborting at 900000ms, or adding an entry to validate.commands? Search: validate watchdog ceiling, LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS digest, stored PASS reuse.

summary: A regression harness that passes when a reviewer runs it by hand is not the same claim as a harness wired into the standing suite.
trigger: A story creates a new packages/main/tests/red/*.mjs harness or a new *-smoke.ts task.
lesson: B-3434's own RED harness went twelve review rounds and four reviewer lanes without anyone noticing it was never registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands. Every checklist selector bound to a DIRECT invocation of the harness by path, so 'the regression passes' and 'the regression is wired into the suite' stayed silently distinct claims, and the repository would not have run it on anyone else's change. Only the full validate run caught it, through the repository's own guard red-b49d4-harness-registration.mjs, which demands every tests/red member be either registered or listed in REGISTRATION_EXCLUSIONS with a stated reason. Two side effects worth knowing: the failure cascades, since red-b49d4-registration-derivation.mjs's DECISION_RECORD_IS_LIVE_AND_AUDITED and NEWCOMER_MIRROR_IS_FAITHFUL rows both go red downstream of the registration failure and all three clear from one line; and REAL_CONFIG_BYTE_UNMODIFIED goes red on any UNCOMMITTED lattice.config.json edit, reporting 'M lattice.config.json' from git status even when the sha is unchanged, so commit the config before running the standing suite.

summary: done_prepare --mergeMain on a hot main can pull another story's change into a file yours owns, zeroing the quorum and forcing a TEST to DEV to REVIEW re-anchor.
trigger: Running done_prepare --mergeMain while other stories are landing on main, especially when your story owns a widely-edited file.
lesson: B-3434 reached TEST with everything green - 41 findings resolved, four lane passes, a full-3x2 quorum, 97/97 validate, a signed delivery check. done_prepare --mergeMain then merged main twice in a row and the second merge brought another story's 32/31-line change into packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts, a file B-3434 owned. storyFilesHash moved, the quorum went to 0/3, every lane pass and the delivery check went stale. quorum_submit refused correctly and in the right words: 'quorum_submit will not fabricate a floor quorum without a real review.' review_run_start is not available in TEST, so the only honest route is story_advance back to DEV then REVIEW - which needs dev_memory_preflight_ack first, and needs lattice dispatch --agentType=lattice-review-<lane> per lane before review_run_start will bind. Scope the re-review to merge INTERACTION rather than a fresh audit: grep the merge diff for your own symbols, check whether the three-way merge silently lost one of your hunks, and re-check any line-number citation in your prose. Before starting, git rev-list --count HEAD..main - if main has stopped moving, the cascade will not repeat.

summary: Across six review rounds the CODE drew zero findings while the author's own audit prose drew nine, each a claim of verification that was never run.
trigger: About to write a sentence into a finding resolution, commit message, scope acknowledgement or story summary asserting that something was verified, that a boundary was exercised, or that a tool behaves a certain way.
lesson: B-9ff1 closed with 65 findings. NOT ONE was against the code. All nine filed during closing review were against the story owner's prose about the code, and the same shape repeated even inside the corrections written to confess the previous instance. The instances: "Verified independently" had checked one of two spec locations and missed the more authoritative one. A correction claimed it was "appended" when finding_resolve --resolution is a plain overwrite with no history field. The replacement "verbatim" block was a RETYPING that silently dropped 377 of 1216 bytes including the original's own honesty caveat - proven a retyping rather than a truncation by the diff SHAPE (three scattered internal deletions plus an em-dash to hyphen substitution; a tool truncation makes one contiguous cut). Five records said "filed as follow-up" when a grep of findings.json and all 348 stories found nothing filed. A correction to finding A was written into finding B, leaving A - the record the follow-up story cites by id - still reading as originally asserted. An attribution credited a reviewer PASS RECORD that never mentioned the catch (it came via the agent's narrative hand-back; the readManifest listed the file under filesTriagedByName, not filesReadFully). And a philosophical justification for skipping work was offered while the mechanical answer sat one command away: checklist_update is simply REFUSED in REVIEW ("Allowed phases: INIT, PLAN, DEV"). THE RULE: before writing any sentence about verification, ownership or tool behaviour into an audit record, run the one command that would falsify it. Nine times out of nine the reviewer ran that command and the author had not. COROLLARY: a claim written next to a field a gate validates gets caught by the machine - quorum_submit refused a note asserting a lane pass was current when it was not - while a claim in prose is only ever caught by a reviewer. That asymmetry is why a lane whose job is auditing the author's statements earns its cost.
reusePrompt: About to write "verified", "filed as follow-up", "appended", or any claim about how a tool behaves, into a finding or summary? Search: audit prose overclaim, run the command that would falsify it.

summary: Five reviewers caught five disjoint defect classes; what produced the value was the question each was asked, not the lane itself.
trigger: Dispatching reviewer lanes for a story, or deciding whether a second/cross-vendor reviewer is worth its cost.
lesson: On B-9ff1: quality found nothing twice but byte-verified a "comment-only" claim and that dist was rebuilt from src; test-coverage found a waiver citing a follow-up task that did not exist, then found that a reviewer-discovered inversion had no committed test; concept found nine defects, all in the author's prose, none in code; behavior found three operator-visible defects the other three could not see; cross-vendor codex found two spec-text defects plus an anti-review directive. Near-zero overlap. A generic "review this" would have returned four passes. WHAT WORKED: ask each lane the INVERSE question - everyone asked whether the specificity rule rejects what it should, and behavior was asked whether it rejects what it should NOT, producing the finding that SIGSEGV/ENOMEM/HTTP 404 are rejected while the vaguer "test failed" is admitted, because character entropy measures alphabet diversity rather than semantic specificity. Ask one lane to audit YOUR resolution texts rather than the code. Explicitly invite overrule ("you are the right lane to overrule me on this") - behavior then verified independently and DECLINED to overrule while still catching a wrong spec line-number citation it could have let pass. Ask a judgement no single finding surfaces ("five findings are deferred to the spec owner; do they collectively amount to this leaf shipping while pushing its own subject matter downstream?"). Name the failure modes that LOOK green: is dist actually rebuilt, do backticks terminate a template literal early. And require mutation proof: quality and codex independently mutated a /tmp copy so all five characterization verdicts held while the ranking changed, proving the fixture pins a property rather than five outcomes. TWO MECHANICS: a lane must DECLINE to record a pass while a blocking finding is open (concept did this three times and it is the only reason the story did not close on false records); and a finding is not finished when filed - ask "what committed test now exists because of it?"
reusePrompt: Dispatching review lanes and wondering how to get more than four rubber stamps? Search: ask the inverse question, invite overrule, audit my prose not the code, mutation proof.

summary: A cross-host quorum binds storyFilesHash and survives other stories landing on main; reviewer Prompt Envelopes are a separate binding that does not.
trigger: A main-merge lands during REVIEW and you are deciding whether the cross-host quorum must be redone.
lesson: I believed and repeatedly asserted that ANY main drift stales the quorum because materialHash is a whole-tree digest. WRONG. There is a drift-accept path: "host verdict ...: materialDigest drift accepted because storyFilesHash matches; re-attestation advisory required". Merging 41 commits of other stories' metadata and non-owned source left fullQuorum 3/3 intact, and quorum_submit REFUSED a resubmit ("the standing quorum ... still drift-accepts because storyFilesHash is unchanged"). What stales a quorum is changing the story's OWN files - your own commits. Reviewer Prompt Envelopes ARE a separate binding and DO go stale on any merge (eligibilityDigest / changedFilesDigest recomputation), so lanes need re-passing even when the quorum lives; do not conflate them, as a whole four-lane round was run here on the false premise that the quorum had died. PROBE with review_escalation_status (ok: true / fullQuorum n/n) before assuming a re-quorum is needed; quorum_submit is non-idempotent and refuses when a valid standing quorum exists. SEPARATELY: story_advance carries a FLAT 900000ms watchdog that a 111-command lattice validate now exceeds (aborted at command 40 of 111 at 907s), while done_prepare gets a config-derived budget. The route through is a standalone `lattice validate` under a raised LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, producing a stored PASS the gate then reuses - and that variable must NEVER be set on a gate command because it is baked into effectiveEnvironmentDigest. Also: verification_evidence_batch_add runs its pinned commands SERIALLY against a 300s no-output watchdog, so a 108-record batch aborts; batch by five.
reusePrompt: Main merged during REVIEW and wondering if the quorum died, or story_advance aborted at 900000ms? Search: quorum drift-accept storyFilesHash, prompt envelope separate binding, standalone validate stored PASS.

summary: CORRECTION superseding a67bb17: its claim that none of B-9ff1 65 findings were against the code is false; only the nine filed in the closing-review round were prose findings.
trigger: About to write a striking COUNT into a lesson, summary or report - "N findings, none against X", "zero regressions", "every one of them".
lesson: SUPERSEDES dev-memory entry a67bb17, which stated a false quantified claim and must not be followed. a67bb17 said: "B-9ff1 closed with 65 findings. NOT ONE was against the code." That is WRONG, caught by the concept lane as B-9ff1:F-066 and verified against findings.json: F-005, F-009, F-018, F-042 and F-060 all carry resolutionType 'fixed' and required code commits, and F-050 is a genuine code-versus-spec divergence. Findings against the code exist among the 65. THE TRUE CLAIM IS NARROWER: the NINE findings filed during the 2026-08-18 CLOSING-REVIEW round were all against the story owner's audit prose rather than the code, and zero code findings were filed in THAT round. That narrower statement is accurate and is what the story summary's pitfalls field already said correctly. I generalised an accurate nine-finding subset to the full 65-finding total. WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN THE OTHERS: the false generalisation was written INSIDE the dev-memory entry whose entire subject is claims wider than the evidence, and it was then repeated to the user three times as 'zero findings against the code'. A wrong lesson is worse than no lesson because the next session retrieves it and acts on it - which is precisely why the reviewer filed it as high rather than letting a tidy narrative stand. THE HABIT TO CARRY: when a review round produces a striking pattern, state the SCOPE the count actually covers - this round, this phase, this file - and never let it inherit the story's lifetime total. Check the count against the artifact (findings.json) before writing it, not after. SECOND CORRECTION, from the test-coverage lane on entry f260849: the flat 900000ms budget is the GENERIC CLI default (done-required-timeout-budget.ts:290) applying to any command other than done_required_validate / done_prepare / live_smoke_transcript - a standalone `validate` invocation shares it too. Calling it 'story_advance's watchdog' reads as story_advance-specific and is terse rather than accurate.

summary: SUPERSEDES a67bb17 and 8d1d2bb: three successive versions of a findings-count claim were each false; ship the query instead of a number.
trigger: About to write any COUNT into a lesson, summary, commit message or report - "N findings", "all of them", "zero X", "every one".
lesson:
SUPERSEDES a67bb17 AND 8d1d2bb. Both are wrong, and so was a third version I nearly wrote. Do not follow either; read this instead. THE CLAIM THAT KEPT BEING WRONG: some version of 'N findings in the closing review, all against the author's prose, none against the code'. Version 1 (a67bb17) said 65 findings, none against the code. Version 2 (8d1d2bb) narrowed it to 'the NINE closing-review findings, all prose, zero code findings'. Three separate lanes independently falsified version 2: test-coverage (F-067), concept (F-068, high) and behavior (F-069). WHAT THE DATA ACTUALLY SAYS, measured rather than recalled, by grouping findings.json on createdAt and grepping resolvedReason for a cited commit: TWENTY findings were filed on 2026-08-18, not nine - concept 11, behavior 4, main 3 (recording the cross-vendor host's findings), test-coverage 2 - and FOUR of them cite a source commit (F-052 and F-053 -> 19aeb9de6, F-059 -> 77a5ffab9, F-060 -> 90c21f7f4). A finding that produced a source commit is not a finding against prose. Version 2 was also self-contradictory: it listed F-050 among the 'prose' nine while F-066's own text called F-050 a genuine code-versus-spec divergence. THE REAL LESSON, which survives without any count: the reviewer lane whose job was auditing the author's STATEMENTS about the code found defects there repeatedly, in a story where the code itself was in good shape. That is worth knowing. The number is not, and every attempt to attach one introduced a new false claim. THE STRUCTURAL FIX - stop restating counts in prose; ship the QUERY so the reader re-derives. For this one:
  python3 -c "import json,re;d=json.load(open('.lattice/story/actives/<id>/findings.json'))['findings'];rows=[(f['id'],f.get('createdAt','')[:10],f.get('agent',''),(re.findall(r'commit ([0-9a-f]{8,})',f.get('resolvedReason') or '') or ['-'])[0]) for f in d];print(len(rows));[print(r) for r in rows]"
A count written into prose is a second copy of a number that lives in an artifact, and it drifts the moment the artifact does - the same defect this repository already learned to avoid in code (derive, do not restate) and which I applied correctly to a test fixture in this very story while failing to apply it to my own sentences three times running. SEPARATE CORRECTION carried forward from F-067: 8d1d2bb also said the flat 900000ms CLI budget applies to any command other than done_required_validate / done_prepare / live_smoke_transcript. That list is wrong - live_smoke_transcript is excluded only CONDITIONALLY (done-required-timeout-budget.ts:279, when args.capture is a string), so in its documented capture-less status mode it takes the flat default like any other command. Do not enumerate that exclusion list from memory; read done-required-timeout-budget.ts around lines 279-290.

lesson: SUPERSEDES a67bb17, 8d1d2bb, e367ec1 and e918048. Read this one. summary: Closeout only converges if every artifact-producing action stops before the next one starts; each write invalidates the bindings made before it.
trigger: Driving a story from DEV through REVIEW to DONE, especially one that merges main or resolves findings during closeout.
lesson: Every commit touching a story-owned file invalidates every reviewer receipt, prompt envelope and evidence binding recorded before it — and a finding-resolution commit, a waiver rewrite and a delivery reviewer writing delivery-check.json all count. B-7dff paid three extra full review rounds to that, twice after I had already written the rule down. Evidence refresh is self-invalidating and can need two passes. A validate or npm test run that overlaps any metadata commit fails with "full-suite identity drift", which reads like a test failure but is not. Working order that converges: merge main first, rebuild so dist matches merged source, re-execute stale evidence, THEN run reviewers, then quorum_submit, then advance, writing nothing in between. quorum_submit needs a current-round pass from every active lane and review_pass_set is REVIEW-only, so submit quorum before advancing to TEST or the lanes strand.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for closeout identity drift or reviewer receipt invalidation before starting any TEST to DONE sequence.

summary: Pinning a verification selector to a prose line containing a count kills the intent permanently once the tree grows past that number.
trigger: Writing checklist userSees text or a verification pin selector during PLAN.
lesson: B-7dff pinned CHK-001:happy:0 to "full-suite: 47/47 passed" and CHK-005:happy:0 to a plan-count line. main later added two suite members and three validate commands, so both selectors became unmatchable and both intents needed permanent waivers — the pins are immutable by design (checklist.ts verificationIntentProtectedPhases blocks edits outside PLAN) and no pin-repair command exists. The same mistake also put an absolute 1006s wall time into an acceptance clause, which a slower host then falsified. Pin a stable marker id emitted by the command (VI-OK STORY-CHKNNN-SOMETHING), never a count, a duration, a jobs value or any prose conclusion line. This has now cost B-49d4, B-8df9 and B-7dff a finding each.
reusePrompt: Before writing a userSees string or a verification selector, search dev-memory for pin selector count.

summary: When a gate refuses, look for the exit the repo already provides before improvising a waiver, a relabel or a new story.
trigger: Any Proof-or-Stop gate refusal during PLAN, REVIEW or closeout.
lesson: Three times in one story the first instinct was worse than what already existed. A waiver was written for a receipt that the documented commandTimeoutMs override could have minted — the override is described in CLAUDE.md, in context from turn one. summary: TEST-to-DONE converges only if EVERY mandatory closeout write happens before the reviewers, including the two that no tool reminds you about.

summary: The convergence breaker gates every takeover-carrying command, so --takeover cannot be used to clear a freeze; borrow the owner session id instead.

lesson: enforceConvergenceBreakerGate returns early only when the command is neither story_advance NOR carries --takeover/--forceTakeover. So story_resume --ack --takeover trips the breaker, while story_resume --ack without takeover trips the owner-lease gate — a deadlock. The escape is to run story_resume from a real TTY with LATTICE_SESSION_ID set to the CURRENT owner session id (session_brief prints it), so no takeover flag is needed and the lease gate passes. isInteractiveAckAllowed also requires a TTY and no CI/LATTICE_AUTOPILOT, so an agent session can never clear a freeze — this is deliberate and must be handed to the human. summary: DONE-required evidence binds the producing process env, so the session that runs done_required_validate must be the one that runs story_advance DONE.

summary: A specific checkable claim written into a durable record without running the check in the reader's context is a defect class of its own, with at least four distinct mechanisms.
trigger: Writing a finding resolution, commit body, code comment, dismissal reason, or summary that states a count, a command, a digest, a listing, or that something was 'filed' or 'recorded'.
lesson: On B-a745 reviewer lanes repeatedly found defects only in the story owner's written claims, never in the code, and the owner repeated the class inside the corrections for it. The mechanisms were distinct and one rule does not cover them: (1) a figure copied from a subagent report and never re-queried; (2) a check that WAS run correctly but was mistranscribed into the record (escaped vs unescaped grep alternation); (3) a category error, citing a session-only referent (a task chip) as if it were a repository filing; (4) a context mismatch, running the check in the main checkout and asserting it for the story worktree; and finally the tally of instances itself became a wrong figure. Two rules that stood up: any check must be run in the story worktree and its literal output pasted into the record, never summarised; and a durable record may cite only artifacts that exist in the repository at write time (story_draft is the durable deferral mechanism when gap_log is unavailable). Both rules apply to commit bodies too, so an implementer dispatch that wants a figure in a commit must require the pasted output there. Never write a count of your own instances into prose; query the ledger when the number is needed.
reusePrompt: About to write a resolution, commit message, comment or summary containing a count, digest, command, listing, or the words filed/recorded/listed? Search: pasted output not summary, artifact exists at write time, no count in prose.

summary: An 'unknown role' or 'promptEnvelope.roles contains unknown role' error from the proof-or-stop CLI can mean the global binary is a stale build resolving into another story's worktree, not a registry defect; and long silent host reviews are killed by the CLI's 5-minute no-output watchdog unless PROOF_OR_STOP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS is raised for that call.
trigger: dispatch or agent_prompt fails with unknown role; cross_host_review or host_run reports stuck after 300 seconds without output.
lesson: Check `node -e "console.log(require('fs').realpathSync(require('child_process').execSync('which proof-or-stop').toString().trim()))"` first: on B-a745 the global proof-or-stop resolved into .worktrees/<other-story>/packages/main/dist/cli.js, a pre-rename build whose templates and ROLE_POLICIES used the old role prefix, so every proof-or-stop-* role name in the post-rename config was 'unknown'. Do not edit role names or add aliases; build the worktree's own dist and run node packages/main/dist/cli.js for every command in that story, and do not repoint the global symlink while another story's session may depend on it. Separately, cross_host_review and host_run run a provider subprocess that is silent for many minutes; the outer CLI watchdog (default 300000 ms idle) kills it and reports 'stuck: 300 seconds without output'. Raise PROOF_OR_STOP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS and PROOF_OR_STOP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS on that invocation only, never on a gate command whose environment digest is bound into evidence. Also: cross_host_review persists only a stdout digest of the provider's findings unless --json is passed; pass --json, and know that the Codex session log under ~/.codex/sessions carries the verbatim verdict if the text is lost.
reusePrompt: proof-or-stop says unknown role, or a host review dies at exactly 300s with no output? Search: stale global binary in another worktree, local dist cli, idle timeout env for host runs, cross_host_review --json.

summary: A commit-subject guard that accepts a RED from merged history must key on story-qualified ids, because CHK-nnn and F-nnn restart per story and any merged RED(CHK-001) would satisfy any later GREEN(CHK-001).

lesson: Only RED(B-xxxx:CHK-nnn) / RED(B-xxxx:F-nnn) subjects may satisfy a GREEN from history, and only when the GREEN carries the same qualified id; unqualified GREENs need an in-range RED or a No-RED: reason of 30+ characters. Read the history with a --grep-bounded git log and an explicit maxBuffer through a strict helper that raises on failure; a null-swallowing helper turned an ENOBUFS into an empty set and silently disabled the allowance on this repository.

summary: A documentation assertion built on a substring check survives deletion of the very sentence it claims to verify; assert the sentence and re-run against a corpus with it removed, requiring failure.
trigger: Writing or reviewing a case that checks documentation content, or any assertion of the form text.includes(SOME_NAME); also when an intent sentence names several clauses but the pinned case tests one.
lesson: Three separate findings in one story came from the same shape. A check for a command name passed even when the explanation around it was deleted, because the name appeared elsewhere in prose. A case-insensitive search for a bound phrase survived deleting the rule sentence, because a pre-mortem row repeated the phrase with different punctuation. Build documentation checks as a corpus of quoted sentences, assert each is present, then re-run the whole check against a copy with that one sentence removed and require the check to fail. Confirm each quoted sentence occurs exactly once in the document it is asserted against, or the mutation proves nothing.

summary: Narrowing a guard by disqualifying a term pair on proximity alone reopens the hole it protects; disqualify only when no decisive relation joins the two terms.
trigger: A guard false-positives on ordinary prose and the quick fix is to stop pairing two specific terms, or to remove a term from a detection list.
lesson: A guard paired a severity subject with a responsibility outcome within a character span, and ordinary prose about story priority tripped it. Disqualifying that one cell cleared the false positive but also admitted Priority alone decides the story, which is exactly what the guard exists to catch; a reviewer proved it by driving the real entry point rather than reading the diff. The correct shape is to disqualify the generic cell only when no decisive relation sits between the terms, reusing the verb vocabulary the file already has for its other detectors rather than inventing a second list. Any such fix needs true-positive fixtures in the same commit, one per axis, or the next reviewer cannot tell a narrowing from a disabling.

summary: A framework guard reading a story checklist can block every reviewer lane at review_run_start, and the checklist context is frozen outside INIT, so the fix belongs in the guard rather than the prose.

lesson: The whole REVIEW phase stops, not one lane, and there is no override on review_run_start. Reopening the story to INIT to reword the text resets non-pending checklist items to pending, so it costs more than fixing the guard. Treat it as acceptance-blocking for the current story and fix the guard in place with a scope acknowledgement, keeping true-positive fixtures. Reviewers that cannot obtain a run id will still do the work and report unsigned; read those reports, but re-run the lanes with signed runs afterwards, because unsigned findings are not gate evidence.

summary: A guard that has never been observed failing is not evidence, and three guards in one story passed on exactly the defect they were written to catch.
trigger: Writing or reviewing a verification script, smoke guard, or contract check that is meant to prove a property.
lesson: Every guard needs a negative control BEFORE it is trusted: inject the exact defect it targets and confirm it fails. In B-3e16 three separate guards passed on their own target defect. verify-docs searched a whole 1400-line file so a deleted flag still matched elsewhere. verify-no-project-writes allowlisted by FILE, so a project-root write in an allowed file passed while printing a reassuring cache-derived reason. verify-clean-tree used the default warm cache, so no index rebuild fired and it measured nothing at all. Each produced specific, confident output. Also beware the control being broken rather than the guard: an `if (false && ...)` neuter can fail to compile and leave a STALE dist that reports PASS, and prefixing a condition into a compound `A || B` disables only A. A neuter must DELETE the check, and you must confirm the build succeeded and the dist actually changed.
reusePrompt: About to trust a verification script, smoke guard, or contract check? Search this before relying on it: negative control, guard passes on its own target defect, stale dist, vacuous guard.

summary: Fixing the demonstrated instance instead of the class produces a guard that is defeated again by the next spelling of the same attack.
trigger: Responding to a reviewer finding about a bypass, especially in a security or provenance check.
lesson: B-3e16 needed five versions of one write guard because each fix closed the instance shown rather than the class. The reviewer named it exactly: the class was never "single-letter alias", it was "the guard trusts the identifier name". Renaming the variable moved the instance and left the trust intact. A lexical rule cannot decide provenance, and worse, it inverted the incentive: it rejected an honestly named cache write while rewarding the rename that defeats it. The fix that held was measuring the EFFECT (run a real scan in a subprocess, hash every path, assert the repository is byte-identical), because that is primitive-agnostic and catches worker threads, child processes and sqlite alike. When a reviewer says a fix is instance-shaped, stop patching and ask what property is actually being asserted.
reusePrompt: Reviewer says a bypass is fixed but the same attack works through a different spelling? Search: instance versus class, lexical rule cannot decide provenance, measure the effect not the call.

summary: effectiveEnvironmentDigest hashes the whole ambient environment minus a deny-list, so per-invocation host/terminal/OTEL variables make a DONE-required receipt unverifiable from any other shell.
trigger: done_prepare or lifecycle_check reports effective-environment-digest-mismatch[N] even though done_required_validate just returned PASS
lesson: The digest is recomputed at read time from the reader's own environment and compared to the value stored in done-required-evidence.json, so ANY ambient value that differs between the writing process and the verifying process breaks it. VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEY_LIST is digest-pinned by VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEYS_DIGEST and must stay byte-stable, so new keys are stripped at the filter seam in effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment (see HOST_LAUNCHER_SESSION_ENV_KEYS) rather than appended to the pinned list. But the leak has a long tail from independent sources: Claude Code (CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET/TOKEN), cmux (CMUX_TERMINAL_LIFECYCLE_ID, CMUX_TAB_ID, CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID, CMUX_PORT*), Alacritty (ALACRITTY_LOG/SOCKET, PID-embedded), tmux (TMUX, PID-embedded), macOS (LaunchInstanceID), and OTEL (TRACEPARENT, whose span-id regenerates per invocation and therefore defeats any deny-list). Do not chase these one at a time: each fix costs a full lane re-earn plus a ~5 minute DONE-required suite. Instead launch BOTH the receipt writer and every later verifier from one identically-stripped environment via an env -u wrapper script; the digest then matches because both sides see the same environment. Verify stability first by running buildDoneRequiredExecutionIdentity twice through the wrapper and comparing effectiveEnvironmentDigest. The architectural fix (allow-list of semantically relevant vars such as PATH/NODE_OPTIONS/CI/locale instead of a deny-list) belongs in its own story.
reusePrompt: Search for effective-environment-digest-mismatch, TRACEPARENT, or done-required receipt unverifiable across shells before adding another key to HOST_LAUNCHER_SESSION_ENV_KEYS.

summary: A DONE-required receipt written by a separate process can never satisfy the DONE gate: writing it auto-commits story metadata, which moves HEAD and invalidates the receipt just written. Only done_prepare, which writes and consumes in one process, converges.
trigger: done_required_validate reports PASS with refusalReasons=none, but lifecycle_check --target=DONE still reports [BLOCKED] done.done-required-validation with effective-environment-digest-mismatch[0],[1]
lesson: Do not chase the digest by hand. The receipt IS valid at the instant it is written (a read inside that same run showed blockers: 0), but done_required_validate auto-commits done-required-evidence.json plus process-events, which moves headHash/materialHash, so the next separate reader recomputes a different identity and rejects it. Any write-then-read cycle across process boundaries therefore oscillates and never converges. The remedy is proof-or-stop done_prepare --mergeMain --refreshStale --validate, which is designed to write AND consume the evidence inside a single process, so the receipt is evaluated before its own metadata commit moves the hashes. This is also why the gate's own next: hint points at done_prepare rather than at re-running done_required_validate. Wasted effort to avoid: I first blamed PROOF_OR_STOP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (removed it, still mismatched), then AI_AGENT/SECURITYSESSIONID (stripped on both sides, still mismatched), then suspected reader non-determinism (false: my node -e probes each carried a different _ last-arg value, which is itself in VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEY_LIST, so the instrumentation perturbed its own input). A brute-force sweep removing each of ~79 env keys produced no match because the cause was never a single key.

summary: The CertificationWindow needs a FINALIZED UNCONSUMED review-inventory receipt, but story_advance --phase=DEV consumes it. Spend receipts on DEV remediation and the window becomes unreachable, since review_inventory_begin is REVIEW-only.
trigger: certification_window_begin fails [pre_cert_inventory_not_finalized] 'No FINALIZED unconsumed Review Inventory receipt is present', and done_required_validate then fails [pre_cert_window_required]
lesson: done_required_validate is an official heavy certification invocation, so whenever doneRequiredCommands is configured it unconditionally calls refuseHeavyCertificationUnlessAdmitted and needs an ADMITTED/RUNNING window. Do NOT conclude from isOfficialHeavyValidateInvocation (which gates only validate --full) that done_required_validate is exempt; it is not. certification_window_begin needs finalizedUnconsumedReviewInventory: state FINALIZED AND no consumedAt on either the epoch or the receipt. The trap is that story_advance --phase=DEV is the remediation path that CONSUMES the receipt, and review_inventory_begin is REVIEW-only, so if you spend every epoch receipt returning to DEV you arrive in TEST with none left and the window is unreachable without another full REVIEW cycle. On B-5a88 receipts RI-091, RI-092 and RI-094 were all consumed that way before the pattern was spotted. Correct order when a story needs both a DEV repair and a certification window: land all repairs in DEV, advance to REVIEW, run the epoch (lanes + critic), review_inventory_finalize, then advance REVIEW->TEST DIRECTLY (that transition does not consume), leaving the receipt available for certification_window_begin in TEST. Ignore the tool's own 'Next: story_advance --phase=DEV' hint at that point, and verify consumedAt is null on both epoch and receipt before advancing.
reusePrompt: certification_window_begin says pre_cert_inventory_not_finalized, or done_required_validate says pre_cert_window_required? Search: finalized unconsumed inventory receipt, REVIEW to TEST does not consume.

summary: Monkeypatching child_process functions with a bare wrapper silently breaks util.promisify(execFile) in every traced descendant because the wrapper drops the util.promisify.custom symbol.
trigger: A test or script that passes standalone fails only under done_required_validate / traced validate with TypeError reading .split or .stdout of undefined, or promisify(execFile) resolves a bare string instead of {stdout, stderr}.
lesson: The runtime tracer (validation-runtime-tracer.cjs) wraps spawn/exec/execFile/fork so traced runs observe process boundaries. exec and execFile carry an own util.promisify.custom symbol property that makes promisify resolve {stdout, stderr}; a plain wrapper function does not inherit own properties, so promisify falls back to the generic form resolving the first callback value (the stdout string), and destructuring {stdout} from a string yields undefined. The fix must copy own property descriptors onto the wrapper AND re-define promisify.custom with a tracing shim, because a plain descriptor copy lets promisified spawns escape the trace entirely. Regression coverage: validation-runtime-tracer-transparency-smoke.ts with a git-show negative control against the pre-fix tracer. General rule: any wrapper that replaces a Node builtin function must preserve its own symbols/properties (promisify.custom, Symbol.toStringTag) or downstream metaprogramming silently degrades only in the instrumented environment - the defect class is invisible to code review and to any test lane that does not run traced.
reusePrompt: traced test fails but passes standalone / promisify execFile resolves string / tracer wrapper transparency / TypeError split undefined under done_required_validate

summary: Registering a new test task requires THREE fail-closed membership authorities, not two; missing the third aborts the entire root suite rather than skipping that task.
trigger: Adding any new test:<name> task, or seeing `npm test` exit 1 within about a second with `canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]`.
lesson: This repo maintains THREE separately-maintained test-membership lists, and none is derived from another: (1) validate.commands in lattice.config.json, (2) the test:<name> script plus its entry in test:serial-reference in root package.json, and (3) RESOURCE_POLICY in packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts. The third is the one people miss and the most punishing to omit: entriesFromSerialReference fails CLOSED, throwing `canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]` at module load, so a serial-reference member with no RESOURCE_POLICY entry takes down `npm test` for the WHOLE repository instead of merely going unrun. Because npm test is a doneRequiredCommands entry, that also blocks done_required_validate and therefore DONE. Use the plain repoRead(name) policy for a task that only reads the repo and spawns the CLI against temp dirs; the name string must match the npm script and task filename exactly. This has now bitten at least four stories (B-cdf6, B-49ed, and B-9f2c twice over, since the decision doc that was supposed to prevent it itself said TWO). Verify with `node -e` calling entriesFromSerialReference directly and asserting unknownPolicy=[] rather than trusting a grep of two files.
reusePrompt: Adding a new test task, or npm test dies in under a second with canonical inventory mismatch / unknownPolicy? Search: three membership authorities, RESOURCE_POLICY fails closed, full-suite-runner.

summary: Signed artifacts auto-commit, so earning them one at a time never converges: batch every mutation first, freeze the tree, then earn all verdicts in one pass.
trigger: Chasing repeated stale_* / review_evidence_invalid / Prompt Envelope invalid blockers where fixing one artifact re-stales another.
lesson: Reviewer passes, verification receipts, delivery checks, rollout reports and scope acknowledgements all bind to the file set AND all auto-commit their own metadata. So any artifact earned before a later mutation is invalidated by that mutation, and earning them serially is a non-convergent loop. The fix is ordering, not retrying: FIRST enumerate every remaining blocker in one read (lifecycle_check --target=DONE lists them all), THEN perform every mutation (phase bounces, code and doc fixes, scope_contract_acknowledge, rollout regeneration, evidence refresh), THEN commit so the tree is frozen, and ONLY THEN earn the signed artifacts — dispatching all reviewer lanes simultaneously against that one commit so their envelopes share a changedFilesDigest. Corollary: reviewer lanes must be earned LAST among signed artifacts, because every other mutation invalidates them. In B-9f2c a doc fix that landed after two lanes had signed invalidated both and cost a full round; batching finished the same work in one. Also give each concurrently dispatched agent a UNIQUE scratchpad filename — two lanes told to use the same payload path overwrote each other mid-flight.
reusePrompt: Stuck in a loop where fixing one gate artifact stales another (stale_delivery_check, invalid_review_run_binding, Prompt Envelope invalid)? Search: batch mutations then freeze then earn, reviewer lanes last.

summary: Acknowledge out-of-scope paths before the first acceptance seal, not when the REVIEW gate asks
trigger: A story commits a fix touching a file outside its signed scope contract
lesson: scope_contract_acknowledge moves the scope-contract digest, which invalidates an already-sealed acceptance-basis (AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING) and pre-review-check (PR_ARTIFACT_TAMPERED). The requirement only surfaces at story_advance REVIEW, so if you seal first you pay the full basis to rollout to live-proof to pre-review rebuild twice. Run scope_contract_check right after any out-of-scope commit and ack immediately. The CLI arg is --paths (JSON array), not --path.

summary: verification_evidence_refresh_stale rebinds hashes but never re-runs the pinned command
trigger: Coverage reads covered=0 after a refresh that printed Refreshed N/N stale evidence items
lesson: Refreshed N/N means REBOUND, not RE-EARNED. Every touched receipt becomes mechanical:false with nonMechanicalReason saying the pinned command was not re-run, and coverageStatusForCoveredEvidence then demotes executable intents to non_mechanical, so covered drops to 0 while every row still says result:pass. To genuinely re-earn, build verification_evidence_batch_add from each intent's own verificationIntent.LANE[i].verification {command,selector} plus its existing kind: one execution fans out to all rows. Two traps: a named intent stores its id as the FULL ref (CHK-001:edge:oversized-output-probe) so a positional loop invents a nonexistent edge:3 and is refused with intent_ref_unresolved -- derive refs from existing verificationEvidence[].intentRef; and preserve each row's original kind instead of overwriting all rows with one value.

summary: Surface the review-assurance floor during REVIEW; on a single host only a human can clear it
trigger: A high-risk story reaches TEST with every mechanical gate green but doneClosure blocked
lesson: The DONE gate requires assurance three-round-two-hosts-or-degraded-single-host. On one machine autopilot_review_status reports independentHosts:0, so the 3x2 path is impossible -- and per-run lines may still read 'pass 2/2 passing hosts', which counts host ENTRIES not INDEPENDENT hosts, so never cite those as satisfying the floor. The only remaining path is review_escalation_fallback_set with eligibility single-host-environment, and cannotAutoSign explicitly bars done_prepare, story_advance and the story owner/main session from writing it. Run review_escalation_status while still in REVIEW so the human approval is requested before everything else is finished and idling.

summary: A temporary filesystem mirror is not Git-isolated if its .git entry points to the real worktree administration.
trigger: Validation reports state_changed_before_launch despite unchanged HEAD and staged file contents while tests create linked repository mirrors.
lesson: Separate raw index bytes from staged-entry content and HEAD when diagnosing causal preflight drift. A mirror that links the real .git can allow ordinary Git commands to update the source index cache. Reproduce the structural shared-administration defect without writing the shared index; then use private admin/index/refs while sharing objects read-only as appropriate, and assert real index bytes, staged entries and HEAD remain unchanged across the complete harness. Preserve the production index guard. A passing standalone run does not identify the historical inner writer or prove that a task-scoped optional-lock setting repaired the defect.

summary: Distinguish causal refusal diagnostics from historical root-cause proof and confirm actual validation recovery.
trigger: A validation run aborts with a shared causal_preflight_refused surface error.
lesson: A shared refusal message does not establish whether owner-lease refresh, preflight signature verification or fact drift failed. Preserve the old log and its uncertainty. Add deterministic negative controls that prove each short-circuit branch and emit only safe reason codes or changed field names, never credential or fact values. Then retain the actual complete validation result separately: diagnostic GREEN does not itself prove operational recovery, and a later successful run does not retrospectively establish the old branch.
